title: Plan a campaign, test small ads and know if you made money
course_title: Digital Marketing Fundamentals for Small Businesses

say: Plan a campaign, test small ads, and know if you made money.
This is the video for module four: campaigns, paid ads, measurement and growth.
A campaign is a focused push with one objective, an offer, a start and end date, and a budget. Write a one-page brief before you spend a naira.
Maryam in Kaduna sells school uniforms. Her objective is 60 orders between 1 and 31 August.

panel.heading: The one-page campaign brief
items: Objective: 60 uniform orders in August
Audience: parents within 5 km of the shop
Offer: free name embroidery before 20 August
Channels: Status, broadcast, a Facebook ad, flyers
Budget and measures: orders, cost per order

say: Keep the offer truthful. No fake countdowns or false only 2 left messages. Once customers catch one false claim, they stop trusting the rest.

say: Maryam works out what success looks like before she starts. These figures are illustrative.
She makes about 3,500 naira profit per order. That is her break-even cost per order. She wants to keep at least half, so her target is 1,750 or less.
She puts about 40,000 into an ad over 3 weeks, and 10,000 into flyers with her WhatsApp QR code.
That is about 50,000 naira. She asks every buyer, where did you see our offer, and labels each chat by source.
Choose the objective that matches the action you want. For WhatsApp sellers, a click-to-WhatsApp ad opens a chat with you.
Amaka tested about 14,000 naira over 7 days, in Port Harcourt, with two ads. The platter photo got 4 orders.

panel.heading: Amaka's two ads: photo or video?

say: The packing video got 9 orders, at about half the cost per order. So she switched off Ad A.
Compare ads by cost per order, not only cost per click. Test with money you can afford to lose.

say: Ngozi spent 30,000 naira on ads for her skincare website, and got 18 purchases. That is about 1,667 naira per purchase.

cards.d: Spend divided by purchases. 30,000 naira for 18 purchases is about 1,667 each.
Revenue from ads divided by ad spend. 216,000 divided by 30,000 is 7.2.
Profit per order before ads was 5,000. Cost per purchase is well below it.

say: Those purchases brought 216,000 naira. Return on ad spend is revenue divided by spend: 7.2.

say: But revenue is not profit. Each order costs her about 7,000 in products, packaging and delivery, so her profit before ads is 5,000.
The rule: if cost per order is below profit per order before ads, the campaign made money.

say: An A/B test compares two versions that differ in one thing. Halima's salon tested two weekday offers.

panel.heading: Run a fair A/B test
items: Change one thing only
Split the audience fairly
Give it enough data, full weeks
Compare rates and write it down

panel.rule: Never click 'Meta support' links. Keep two-step verification on.

say: Use cost per order against break-even to decide. Raise budgets in steps, because sudden jumps can push costs up.
And doubling orders is only good if you can still deliver on time.

panel.heading: Stop, keep or scale
items: Well above break-even: stop or change one big thing
Below break-even and steady: keep testing
Well below for weeks: raise budget gradually
Frequency rising, results falling: refresh
Check you can still deliver on time

say: Keeping a customer is cheaper than winning one. Bisi earns about 3,000 naira profit per meal-pack order.

panel.heading: Why a regular customer is worth so much

say: To remember. Write a brief with an honest offer. Test small, and compare ads by cost per order.
Check profit, not just revenue. Change one thing at a time, and grow gradually.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Write a one-page brief with an honest offer
Test small, with money you can afford to lose
Compare by cost per order, not cost per click
Profit, not revenue, tells you if ads worked
Change one thing at a time; scale gradually
